scene kirinthinking1
So begins another day beside a calculated disaster.
I wasn’t particularly fond of that title when I first heard it in Kirin’s dorm room, but after putting a bit more thought into it, I think it works quite well.
In a sense, I’m also a calculated disaster of sorts.
And no, that is not another excuse for me to be self-deprecating. I already have plenty of those.
It’s a fair evaluation based on my tendency to change or mold myself to fit the ideals of those around me.
But I’ve never been fond of changing, so the transformation is always a bit incomplete.
Imagine you buy sixteen puzzles, all with at least one or more pieces missing. (It was a really shitty puzzle store.)
And you have a friend who makes puzzles for a living.
An enigmatologist, if you will.
The enigmatologist says to you-
“I can likely craft you the missing piece based on a description of it, but there is a chance the size will be slightly off without the proper schematics.”
Of course, that problem could be easily remedied if you’d just bring him the puzzle so he can figure out exactly what it is that’s needed.
But you’re a fucking lazy dick and don’t want to be bothered making a second trip.
So you have him guess and ultimately wind up with a piece that is slightly off.

But you still take it from him and just mash it into the puzzle anyway, not caring if it causes the rest to snap or break or whatever it is that happens when you try to solve a puzzle with brute force.
And everything comes falling down.
Everything but me, that is.
For I am both the enigmatologist as well as the one who was too lazy to ever provide the schematics.
I am both the cause of all problems as well as their respective solution.
A makeshift god who can provide temporary solace, but never truly guide someone toward salvation.
And as long as puzzles with missing pieces exist, I will continue to ruin them.
Because an enigmatologist does not just create puzzles, they solve them as well.
And if all of the puzzles in all of the world are solved, what is left for me to do?
Break puzzles to make new puzzles.
Fuck it. Take every puzzle you bought from that shitty store and dump the contents into a giant bowl.
Maybe even a well.
Create the ultimate puzzle.
Solve it.
Become God.
Thank you for once again listening to my incessant ramblings about all that is broken and how to both fix and unfix it.
: So...I’m thinking about quitting the team.
: Is this about the sit-ups again?
: Nah.
: Frankly, I was a little more disappointed that Miku wouldn’t let you into the showers with us despite clearly wanting it.
: So Miku’s prudence is the reason you’re thinking of quitting?
scene kirinthinking2
: Nah.
: I’m just thinking it might be time to move onto something I’m a little better at.
: Like, I’ve been playing soccer for pretty much my entire life and have always been a middle-of-the-road player at best.
: I still think it’s fun and everything, but it gets kind of annoying at times.
: Like, you try so hard to improve...only to watch everyone else get better without putting in even half of the effort.
: I don’t really think it’s fair to say that they’re putting in less effort when, more often than not, it’s the two of us up here rather than them.
scene kirinthinking3
: Who says that I don’t spend every waking moment outside of practice practicing?
: I think you might have the wrong idea of what “practice” and “outside of practice” are supposed to consist of.
: Maybe I just like practicing alone better?
: Because you’re self-conscious?
scene kirinthinking4
: What’s wrong with being a little self-conscious?
: I’m a [teenage]girl surrounded by other [teenage]girls who are naturally better at almost everything than me.
: Of course I’m going to be self-conscious.
: Do you think that makes me weak, Sensei?
: No. I think it makes you human.
: Which is a good thing because I’ve definitely questioned that about you on several occasions.
scene kirinthinking5
: What else would I be if not a human?
: A puzzle.
: Like a jigsaw puzzle or...a crossword puzzle?
: Whichever one is harder for the average person to solve, I guess.
: Probably a jigsaw puzzle, then. Those can get kind of intense once you start adding a bunch of pieces.
: But I guess crossword puzzles can also get intense once you start adding crazy words like-
: Enigmatology?
scene kirinthinking6
: Yeah. Whatever that is.
: How is anyone supposed to guess a word that they’ve never even heard before?
: I mean, I guess it’s easier now since we all have access to the Internet, but still. That’s way too much work.
scene kirinthinking7
: See that girl with the crazy thighs over there? The one with the ball in her hands?
: That is your sister, Karin. I am quite familiar with her.
: Yeah, whatsherface.
: She and I actually used to team up and put jigsaw puzzles together when we were little. Like, way before we were even in elementary school.
: Neither of us were particularly good at them on account of being stupid little kids but, just like with soccer, she got better and I lagged behind.
: Now, this club is pretty much the only thing the two of us ever do together.
: So you can probably guess how that makes me feel.
: Not really any point in guessing when you’re already making it extremely apparent.
scene kirinthinking8
: Hey, when a puzzle gets too hard, what do you do?
: Do you give up?
: Or do you keep working at it no matter how tough it gets?
: No clue. But I’ll let you know how I feel the next time something like that happens to me.
: Bummer.
: I was hoping to find out what you’re planning on doing with me.
: You know, since I’m just as much of a puzzle as I am a human being to you.
: Once you’ve got all the outer pieces put together, are you really going to go through all of the effort to finish the rest?
: Or are you just going to call it quits and move onto another?
: I mean, we all know the outer part of the puzzle is the most fun. So why bother doing the rest when there are puzzles literally everywhere?
: What would the equivalent of that be if we’re counting you entirely as a person and not an object?
scene kirinthinking9
: I guess it would be just...getting close enough to fuck me, proceeding to actually fuck me, and then running off to fuck somebody else when you realize I’m not worth fucking anymore.
: Or something.
: So it all comes back to sex.
: It all comes back to sex.
: I mean, that’s how our relationship started, wasn’t it?
: A promise that you could have what you want from me as long as I can have what I want from you.
: Luckily, we both want the same thing now.
: Who’s to say either one of us will want to finish the rest of the puzzle once the outline is done?
: Sure, I guess there’s some momentary satisfaction once you actually solve a puzzle.
: But after that, you just break it apart and put it back in the box or use that weird puzzle glue to hang it on the wall or the fridge.
: I don’t think you’d look particularly nice hanging on my wall.
: I don’t even think you’d fit on my wall.
: Hell, I’m not even sure if you’ll fit in me.
: So it all comes back to sex.
: It all comes back to sex.
scene kirinthinking10
Kirin looks away from me, watching the rest of the girls practice.
I can’t say for certain, as I still haven’t completed her outline, but I’m pretty sure she’s hoping that one of them looks over at her right now.
That someone smiles and coaxes her into coming down and practicing with them instead of abandoning her atop this stage filled with athletic bags and traffic cones.
At the same time, though, Kirin abandoned them.
They’ve abandoned each other, so it wouldn’t make any sense for one of them to reach out.
It’s just an unfortunate yet realistic progression of one’s interests and confidence dwindling with the passage of time.
Time is the worst.
: Maybe I’ll just find something to do with Noriko.
: She’s fun to be around. And she’s yet to make me feel insignificant, so that’s pretty sweet.
: You two are still getting along?
scene kirinthinking11
: We’re kind of like two sides of the same coin.
: We’ve got our differences and will probably never have the same exact mindset as one another, but we’re still out to do the same thing at the end of the day.
: Is that “thing” having sex with me?
scene kirinthinking12
: I was talking more about filling a void in our hearts, but I guess the sex thing is also true.
: Am I just a tool to you?
scene kirinthinking13
: You’re kind of a tool in general.
: I did not come here to be insulted.
: A useful tool. Like a hammer or a...chainsaw.
: Or a vibrator.
: I guess it’s your turn to turn everything sexual now?
: You did it twice in a row earlier, so now I have to catch up.
: From this point on, it’s anyone’s game.
scene kirinthinking14
: That aside, things have definitely started to look up a bit since Noriko and I moved in together.
: I always knew getting out of my parents’ house would be great for me, but combining that with a cool, new roommate and a teacher I actually like-
: So it all comes back to sex...
: Stop fucking saying that when I’m trying to hand you a puzzle piece.
: Oh, we’re working together now?
: I just thought we were solving our own puzzles in the same room as one another.
scene kirinthinking15
: Doesn’t mean we can’t check in on each other’s progress every now and then.
: Basically, I’m just saying that life is changing for me.
: Still have no clue if it’s a good change or a bad one, but it’s definitely something. And I’ve been dying for something for years.
scene kirinthinking16
: Thanks a lot for being such a horrible person. I was starting to think other people like me didn’t exist.
: Oh, we’re everywhere. You just need to figure out how to identify us.
: I found out how to identify you pretty easily. Just had to lift my skirt and offer up my v-card.
: Pretty sweet deal in exchange for being able to feel my heart beat again, don’t you think?
: Hopefully I’ll be able to feel that someday too.
: My heart or yours? Cause you can touch my chest pretty much any time you want. Just not sure if this is the best place for it and all.
: I meant mine. But I will gladly grope you in front of any amount of girls.
: Grope away, good sir.
scene black
I reach out for Kirin’s chest.
She closes her eyes and-
: S-Sensei! The heck are you doing over there?!
: Trying to feel whole again.
: Help! I’m being assaulted!
: You fucking traitor.
: Miku! Come save me!
: Sensei! Start doin’ ‘yer job and put all those friggin’ traffic cones back into the storage room!
: Why did you even bring them onto the stage if you weren’t going to use them?
: Ahh...Sensei...
: And why is Kirin making these noises?
: Because you’re grabbin’ her friggin’ boob! Girls react to stuff like that!
: This is a thing I absolutely did not know as it is my first time ever touching a woman and has definitely never happened before this moment in time.
: I don’t care how many times it’s happened, I-
: Well, actually...I think I kinda do care.
: But just let her go and do ‘yer job!
I [[reluctantly] listen to Miku and stop groping Kirin.
She winks at me before adjusting her bra and skipping over to Miku in the middle of the gym.
I wonder if she’s actually going to follow through with quitting the team or if that was just another one of many of her momentary lapses in judgement.
But I guess there’s no way of knowing without waiting to see how things play out.
Until then, I will keep solving puzzles.
Or creating them.
Or all of the above.
